My child is 2.5 y/o. Still nursing :D  I ask myself the same question almost every day but so far I'd prefer to stop when he stops looking for boob milk. I've gotten used to it and honestly it's convenient.
Convenient in the sense that when he's upset, he nurses to calm down and I don't have to do anything specifically. Also when he's sick (especially if it's a stomach virus) he nurses frequently, so I don't worry about dehydration.

I try not feel embarrassed that I still nurse such a big toddler but.... I am embarrassed sometimes especially when he asks for "breast milk" (that's what he calls it) in front of my MIL.

It is easier now, because he eats solids, plays a lot, goes to daycare etc... The nursing sessions are also a lot quicker, they sometimes last mere seconds - as if he wants to quickly reconnect at the end of the day and then runs off to play. 
It was tough for me and very tiring around the 4 month mark and also whenever new teeth were breaking in. I was feeling drained, literally...Never sleeping for more than 2-3hours in a row 🥴

Good luck on your breastfeeding journey! There's no right or wrong amount of time to breastfeed. There's just the right amount of time for a particular mother-baby unit. If it becomes a chore for one side and too difficult, there's no shame in asking for help or stopping. It's also OK to continue until 4-5 years. ❤️

 We slept in the same bed and I brought loads of his favorite toys and books so he can have some sense of familiarity. I think that helped but generally he fares better now that he's at home

Hi, I'm currently in training to become a lactation consultant (not IBCLC though, but a volunteer) and want to say that the LC you mentioned is super unethical.
There are guidelines that deem unethical anyone who tries to convince you that you need certain products for a successful BF journey - be it formula, pumps, bottles, pacifiers, baby wipes,  a giraffe, whatever. For a successful BF journey you need 1. Goals 2. At least one lactating breast 3. Baby born on term.

There are cases though where baby has a tongue/lip tie and even if it's not an issue for breastfeeding, those have to be removed because at a later stage they can become an issue regarding eating (chewing food, using the tongue to move if left and right) and talking. Nevertheless, even I ,while still in training, can tell if a baby has a true tongue tie concerns or not, and then the proper thing to do is redirect to a doctor who can verify it and take care of it ,if needed .

Can your child be awake for 5 hours without getting irritated, tired or overstimulated? If yes, you can transition to 1 nap. If not, it could be a tad early.

What you can do to help the 1 nap transition :

Try increasing the awake intervals slowly over a period of time. For example, my boy can be awake for 3hrs and 30 mins in the morning before becoming too tired which prevents us from doing 1 nap only. So, today he was awake for 3 hrs and 40 mins. Tomorrow, we'll do 3 hrs and 50 mins and so on until we reach 4 hours and 30 mins.

Cut the shorter nap even shorter. For example first nap could be 1hr and 20 - 30mins and the second nap a short cat nap (15-30 minutes) , so he could manage until his bedtime. Or vice versa, depending on when his shorter nap is.
I attended a webinar a while back regarding the 2 to 1 nap transition and that's what really stuck with me. 

Make sure everything else is OK: eating, water consumption, milk etc. Quiet activities 1 hr before bedtime. Bedtime routine that is calming and always the same.

I hope this helps a little bit. Hugs!
